subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Which failure-policy path should be canonical for this issue: runtime skip for timeout/true retryable 429/5xx, UI recovery from preflight dispatch errors, or both?
rationale: The source bug is real, but broad fail-open behavior can mask provider/auth/billing setup errors, and three open PRs currently compete on the retryability boundary.

options.title: Canonical runtime retryability contract
options.body: Use timeout, true retryable 429, and 5xx as skipped guardrail outcomes while keeping 400/401/403 and billing/operator-action failures terminal, with real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: UI recovery first
options.body: Keep preflight failure policy mostly terminal and make the Control UI recover the Composer with a clear retry/error state when preflight dispatch fails.

options.title: Combined fix
options.body: Land a narrow runtime retryability contract plus a UI safety net, accepting the broader review surface and requiring proof for both paths.

recommendation.title: Canonical runtime retryability contract
recommendation.body: Use timeout, true retryable 429, and 5xx as skipped guardrail outcomes while keeping 400/401/403 and billing/operator-action failures terminal, with real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle gave the most recent concrete retryability-boundary feedback on the related PR and is connected to the current released source snapshot.
